_meta.indication: In combination with doxorubicin, for the treatment of adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS) with a histologic subtype for which an anthracycline-containing regimen is appropriate and which is not amenable to curative treatment with radiotherapy or surgery.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), active-controlled trial of olaratumab plus doxorubicin versus single-agent doxorubicin.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with advanced soft tissue sarcoma (STS) who had not previously received an anthracycline.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by the investigator per RECIST v1.1; overall survival (OS) was a secondary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: 133 patients (66 olaratumab plus doxorubicin, 67 single-agent doxorubicin)
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 6.6 vs 4.1 months (stratified HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.44, 1.02; two-sided p=0.06); median OS 26.5 vs 14.7 months (unstratified HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.34, 0.79; p<0.05); confirmed ORR by BICR 18.2% vs 7.5%.

key_safety: Major safety concern is serious infusion-related reactions (IRR: 12.6% any grade, 3.1% Grade 3-4 in the combination arm). Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were nausea, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, mucositis, alopecia, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, abdominal pain, neuropathy, and headache. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was increased with the combination (47% vs 37%).
target_moa: Olaratumab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFR-alpha), a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed on cells of mesenchymal origin whose signaling plays a role in cell growth, chemotaxis, and differentiation.

rems.type: A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is not recommended based on the current safety profile of olaratumab.

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of Lartruvo for treatment of adult patients with STS.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Accelerated approval was based on the overall survival and PFS benefit in the small Trial JGDG, with residual uncertainty regarding the magnitude and breadth of clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The recommendation for accelerated approval rather than regular approval is based on the uncertainty of the magnitude and breadth of the clinical benefit of overall survival and PFS given the small numbers of patients, heterogeneous patient population, and statistical considerations discussed in Section 7.4.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Conduct and submit the results of a multicenter, randomized clinical trial (Trial JGDJ) confirming the clinical benefit of olaratumab in combination with doxorubicin in patients with soft tissue sarcoma that is not amenable to surgery or radiation.

summary.text: Lartruvo received Fast track (08/21/2014), Orphan Drug (10/09/2014), Breakthrough designation with rolling review, and Priority review, and was granted accelerated approval based on the OS and PFS benefit seen in the small Trial JGDG, with a required confirmatory randomized trial (Trial JGDJ) to verify clinical benefit.
